newsitem.title: ITALY: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN AND KOSTNER SHARE VICTORY.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-ZURBRIGGEN AND KOSTNER SHARE VICTORY.

text.p: Switzerland's Heidi Zurbriggen, who considered retiring last year, and Italian Isolde Kostner on Friday became the first Alpine skiers in 30 years to share victory in a women's World Cup downhill.
The two clocked identical times of one minute 30.81 seconds down the 2,490-metre Olimpia delle Tofane piste.

"It's nice to be alone on the podium but sharing it is fine," said Kostner after her first victory of the season gave the Italian women three wins in four races -- an ideal preparation for the world championships at home next month.
Germany's Katja Seizinger, winner of the opening downhill of the season in Lake Louise, was third in one of the closest finishes ever, two hundredths of a second behind.
The German lost her lead in the World Cup downhill standings to Zurbriggen, who now has 269 points to Seizinger's 266.
But there was some consolation for the Olympic downhill champion, who narrowed the gap in the overall World Cup standings to 304 points behind Sweden's Pernilla Wiberg.
Wiberg, who had been chasing her first career downhill victory and was 328 points ahead of defending champion Seizinger before Friday's race, finished seventh in 1:31.38.
It was only the sixth time in World Cup history that a race had been tied and, curiously, the last such occurrence was on the same Cortina piste in a women's super-G in 1994.
The only other time that a women's downhill had been shared was in Sestriere, Italy, in 1967 when Italy's Giustina Demetz and Marielle Goitschel of France tied.

Kostner, who won one of two downhills here early last year before going on to become super-G world champion, started immediately after Zurbriggen and was 0.36 seconds ahead at the first intermediate timing but then faded.
The double Olympic bronze medallist was just 0.08 seconds ahead at the second intermediate.

"This win came at just the right moment, to give me back my confidence for Sestriere," said the Italian, whose downhill season so far has disappointed some fans but who placed second in a super-G in Bad Kleinkirchheim, Austria, this month.
The Italian resort of Sestriere hosts the world championships from February 2 to 16.
Zurbriggen, sister of former Olympic and world champion Pirmin, had won only once before -- at Lillehammer last year -- going into this season but this was her second consecutive win in a month.
The veteran Swiss, who will be 30 in March, won the last fog-hit downhill in Bad Kleinkirchheim.
"I can't really explain my good form now," the Swiss said, before proceeding to do just that.
"My brother helped me to find a new position on my skis and we worked a lot on my boots," she said.
Pirmin, who won 40 World Cup races in his time as one of the sport's greatest all-rounders, has been helping his sister.
Heidi Zurbriggen said after winning in Bad Kleinkirchheim that her new, harder boots allowed her to corner faster and were cutting her times by an average of around half a second.
Friday's race was briefly halted after American Megan Gerety, the 16th starter, crashed heavily coming off a jump at high speed and careered into the safety netting.
The fall came near the point where Germany's giant slalom World Cup champion Martina Ertl crashed in training on Thursday, ending her world championship hopes.
Officials said Gerety was shaken but not seriously injured and she skied back down to the finish area later.
Cortina hosts a women's super-G on Saturday, followed by a giant slalom on Sunday.
